name: every non-OK status is recorded as a failure
why: The distinction the whole feature rests on. A 404 means the archive HAS no artwork for that release, which is the commonest case there is — recording it too would put a ⚠⟳ carrying a large number on almost every page, which is the same as having no signal at all.
grep: a 503 is recorded as a failure

name: a transient failure is not recorded at all
why: The pre-F7 state: ctx.countCache holds a zero for both a 404 and a 503 and nothing can tell them apart, so there is nothing for a failed-only control to read. This is the blocker the org called hard.
grep: a 503 is recorded as a failure

name: a successful answer leaves the entity on the failed list
why: The record has to come off when the entity is answered. Only observable on the NETWORK-ERROR branch: a thrown request caches no zero, so an ordinary re-render retries the entity and the success arm is what clears the record. The failed-only RETRY path cannot show it — that one empties the set up front, whether or not the success arm does its job, which is why an earlier version of this entry passed.

name: the retry does not clear the cached zero
why: F5 kept the in-memory zero for a transient failure on purpose, so Tier 1 serves it back on every re-render. A retry that re-arms the anchors without dropping that zero makes no request at all — the same defect F5 itself fixed one layer down, where _artRetryTable() cleared the session caches but not the IDB record.

name: the retry re-arms every entity, not just the failed ones
why: KNOWN GAP, and it corrected my own understanding of the code: this membership test is an EFFICIENCY guard, not the correctness one. Re-arming an anchor only causes a request when the entity has no cache entry, and the entities that answered still have theirs — so Tier 1 serves them and the request counts do not move. What actually limits the requests is the cache-deletion loop above, which IS scoped to `paths` and DOES have a failing mutation ("the retry does not clear the cached zero"). Dropping this test would still make the pass walk every anchor on the page and re-enrich every table, which is worth keeping and is not worth a request-count assertion.

name: the record is cleared after re-enriching instead of before
why: _artEnrichIcon() re-adds any entity that fails a second time. Clearing afterwards wipes that fresh record, so a retry into a still-broken archive reports everything recovered. KNOWN GAP recorded honestly: this fixture lets the retry succeed, so no second failure is produced and the ordering cannot be observed. Covering it needs a route that keeps failing across a retry AND a settled assertion afterwards.
